title: Grounded computer remote tools are defined but omitted from exports and model mapping
reasoning: RemoteGroundedMouseTool and RemoteGroundedScrollTool are concrete remote tool classes, but the package initializer imports and exports only the older computer tool classes, and the local computer-use model map also omits the grounded tool names. Consumers that discover remote tools through the package exports or the computer-use mapping will not see these grounded tools even though the classes exist, which can cause schema/catalog drift between backend prompt/tool exposure and frontend executable capabilities.
recommendation: Either wire the grounded remote tools into the same export and model-mapping paths as the other computer tools, or remove the dead classes if grounded actions are intentionally unsupported through this remote_tools surface.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked catalog or export parity tests are included, and the omission is visible only by comparing the class definitions with the export and mapping lists.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a remote tool catalog parity test that asserts every concrete RemoteToolBase computer class intended for use is discoverable through the package/catalog path and any computer-use model mapping.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/tools/remote_tools/__init__.py, backend/src/tools/remote_tools/computer.py, and a focused catalog/export parity test.
